chosen_translation: I like my job.
rejected_translation: To me my work is pleasing.
defect_description: literal мне нравится dative; 'I like' is natural

chosen_translation: We have a tough week ahead.
rejected_translation: To us there is ahead a hard week.
defect_description: literal нам предстоит dative; word order and construction unnatural

chosen_translation: I have a meeting at three.
rejected_translation: At me a meeting at three.
defect_description: у меня = 'I have', not 'at me'

chosen_translation: My colleagues congratulated me on my promotion.
rejected_translation: Colleagues congratulated me with the promotion.
defect_description: поздравить с = 'congratulate on', not 'congratulate with'

chosen_translation: He can't get the hang of this task.
rejected_translation: To him this task is not given.
defect_description: impersonal не даётся = 'can't manage'; literal dative construction

chosen_translation: The boss is on a business trip.
rejected_translation: The head is in a command trip.
defect_description: начальник = 'boss/manager'; командировка = 'business trip', not 'command trip'

chosen_translation: Lunch is from eleven to twelve.
defect_description: обед = 'lunch', not 'dinner'; 'until' is awkward when 'to' works better

source: Я работаю в офисе два года.
chosen_translation: I have been working in this office for two years.
rejected_translation: I work in office two years.
defect_description: ongoing from past needs present perfect continuous; missing 'the' and 'for'

chosen_translation: The letter was sent on time.
defect_description: missing article 'the'; 'in time' means 'before it was too late', while 'on time' means 'at the scheduled moment'

chosen_translation: All the documents are in order.
defect_description: plural 'documents' requires 'are', not 'is'

source: Она проработала в компании пять лет.
chosen_translation: She worked at the company for five years.
rejected_translation: She worked in company five years.
defect_description: wrong preposition 'in' for company; missing 'the' and 'for'

chosen_translation: The meeting started on time.
rejected_translation: The meeting have started on time.
defect_description: singular subject 'meeting' requires 'started' or 'has started', not 'have started'

chosen_translation: The report is not ready yet.
defect_description: missing article 'the' and copula 'is'

chosen_translation: Thirty people work in the office.
defect_description: 'human' is wrong; 'people' needed; missing articles

chosen_translation: The task was completed on time.
defect_description: срок = 'deadline/schedule', not 'term'; missing article and auxiliary

chosen_translation: We have no vacancies.
rejected_translation: At us there are no vacancies.
defect_description: у нас = 'we have'; 'at us' is literal and ungrammatical

chosen_translation: Send me the file by email.
rejected_translation: I demand you transmit the digital file to me via electronic correspondence.
defect_description: formal/bureaucratic for a casual work request

source: Закрой проект, нам не нужны ошибки.
chosen_translation: Wrap up the project, we don't need any errors.
rejected_translation: Terminate the project initiative in order to avoid erroneous outputs.
defect_description: formal/bureaucratic for an everyday work instruction

chosen_translation: Can you call me a bit later?
rejected_translation: Would it be possible for you to contact me at a later point in time?
defect_description: overly formal for a casual phone request

chosen_translation: I'm busy until five.
rejected_translation: I am preoccupied with matters until seventeen hundred hours.
defect_description: military time format and 'preoccupied' for a simple casual statement

chosen_translation: Let's discuss this tomorrow.
rejected_translation: I propose that we engage in a discussion pertaining to this matter on the morrow.
defect_description: archaic formal for a simple work suggestion

chosen_translation: The colleagues are fine with it.
defect_description: 'not contra' is Latin borrowing not used in English; 'fine with it' is natural

chosen_translation: Work is in full swing.
defect_description: кипеть = 'boil' literally; in this context 'work is in full swing' is the idiomatic equivalent

chosen_translation: Nothing has changed; we are back to square one.
defect_description: literal 'cart still there'; Russian proverb means the problem is unresolved; English 'back to square one'

source: Работа не волк, в лес не убежит.
chosen_translation: Work will wait; there's no hurry.
rejected_translation: Work is not a wolf, it won't run into the forest.
defect_description: literal translation of Russian proverb; English equivalent: 'work will wait'

chosen_translation: To give one's word.
defect_description: дать слово = 'give one's word (to promise)'; 'the word' is not idiomatic in this context

chosen_translation: He is a jack of all trades.
rejected_translation: He is a master for all hands.
defect_description: мастер на все руки = 'jack of all trades'; literal translation is unrecognisable

chosen_translation: This is my specialty.
defect_description: специализация = 'specialization' in academic sense; in casual context 'specialty' is more natural

chosen_translation: This is a promising position.
defect_description: перспективный = 'promising/with potential'; 'perspective' is a false cognate meaning 'point of view'

chosen_translation: He is an experienced specialist.
defect_description: опытный = 'experienced'; 'exited' is not an adjective meaning experienced

chosen_translation: The project was successfully completed.
defect_description: реализован = 'implemented/completed'; 'realized' in English means 'understood', not 'completed'

chosen_translation: This is a current issue.
defect_description: актуальный = 'current/pressing'; 'actual' is a false friend meaning 'real'

chosen_translation: The deadline is tomorrow, hurry up!
defect_description: omission of the urgency instruction 'hurry up'

chosen_translation: The task is done but with a delay.
defect_description: omission of the qualifier 'but with a delay'

chosen_translation: He is a good specialist but slow.
defect_description: omission of the contrasting quality 'but slow'

chosen_translation: Please send your CV and references.
defect_description: omission of the second requested item 'and references'

chosen_translation: Despite the efforts, the project failed.
defect_description: omission of the concessive phrase 'despite the efforts'

chosen_translation: The project was put on hold.
defect_description: замороженный проект = 'project put on hold'; 'frozen project' is literal and less idiomatic

chosen_translation: The salary has been paid.
rejected_translation: The salary has been paid out.
defect_description: 'paid' is natural; 'paid out' implies disbursement from a fund, slightly formal

chosen_translation: He resigned voluntarily.
defect_description: уволиться = 'resign' (leave voluntarily); 'dismissed' means terminated by employer

chosen_translation: He was promoted.
defect_description: повысить в должности = 'promote'; 'raised in position' is literal and unnatural

chosen_translation: There is an urgent meeting at ten in the morning.
rejected_translation: An emergency assembly at ten in the morning.
defect_description: срочное = 'urgent', not 'emergency'; совещание = 'meeting', not 'assembly'

chosen_translation: The agreement has been signed by both parties.
rejected_translation: The contract has been signed by both sides.
defect_description: договор = 'agreement/contract'; стороны in legal context = 'parties', not 'sides'

chosen_translation: The problem was solved.
defect_description: решить проблему = 'solve a problem'; 'decided' is for decisions, not problem resolution

chosen_translation: A competitor entered the market.
rejected_translation: A competitor went out to the market.
defect_description: выйти на рынок = 'enter the market'; 'went out to the market' implies a physical trip

chosen_translation: The company is expanding.
defect_description: расширяться = 'expand' for organisations; 'widening' is physical width, not business growth

chosen_translation: The application was submitted on time.
rejected_translation: The statement was submitted on time.
defect_description: заявление = 'application' (job/official); 'statement' is a financial/legal document

chosen_translation: The client was satisfied.
defect_description: 'remained pleased' oddly implies prior dissatisfaction; 'was satisfied' is natural

chosen_translation: He holds a management position.
defect_description: руководящий = 'management/managerial'; 'occupies' for positions is unusual; 'leading post' is archaic

chosen_translation: The negotiations went well.
defect_description: переговоры прошли = 'negotiations went'; 'passed' implies going through a point, not conducting
